title: observability: token-kv cost/latency dashboards and alert tuning enhancements
author: Maya Patel
body: Context: production teams reported poor visibility into per-token KV cache behavior and unit economics for high-throughput workloads. This PR adds token-level KV cache metrics, expanded cost/latency breakdowns, Grafana dashboard panels, tracing span refinements, and tuned alerts to reduce noisy pages. Motivation: make it straightforward to identify cache-induced latency regressions, quantify per-token cost impact when caching/quantization changes are rolled out, and reduce paging noise by using adaptive thresholds and refractory windows. Summary of changes: 1) runtime: add new Prometheus counters and histograms (kv_cache.hit_count, kv_cache.miss_count, kv_cache.get_latency_seconds, token_per_cost_cents histogram by model+route+quantization); 2) tracing: add span annotations for kv.lookup and kv.fetch, and emit cache-hit/miss tag for root request span; 3) dashboards: new Grafana dashboard token_kv_cost_latency_overview.json with breakdowns (per-model, per-route, per-quantization, prefix-length buckets) and a summarized cost table for the top 50 routes; 4) alert tuning: replace single global alert with route-level alerts using adaptive error budgets and sliding windows; add refractory period to token-latency-high alert; 5) logging: structured logs for cache miss hotkeys and sample stack traces for hotkey detection; 6) tests: unit tests for metric registration and integration test for new dashboard panels using snapshot JSONs; 7) docs: updated observability runbook and dashboard README. Checklist: - [x] Add metrics and histograms - [x] Update tracing instrumentation - [x] Add Grafana dashboard JSON and provisioning - [x] Alert tuning and playbook updates - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Backwards-compatible metric names and feature flag for rollout Impact/risk: low risk to runtime (metrics/tracing are opt-in behind feature flag), dashboards safe to deploy; alert tuning reduces pages and should be monitored for missed incidents. Rollout plan: enable metrics behind FF observability.kv_token_metrics for Canary; roll dashboards to staging; enable alerts in small set of oncall groups for 48h before global enable. Related: ENG-7241 (token-level observability initiative), ENG-7430 (kv cache visibility), SUP-2192 (customer incident referencing noisy token-latency alerts).

review_comments: Aiden Chen: Please avoid adding a new global metric with duplicate labels; can we collapse model+quantization into a single label to avoid high-cardinality?
Maya Patel: Good catch - reduced to model_and_quant label and added cardinality bounds in registry.go; also gated by feature flag.
Sofia Martinez: The refractory window looks reasonable but add a note in the runbook about when to reduce the window for rapid rollback.
Maya Patel: Added runbook section with rollback steps and sample PromQL queries to validate alert coverage.
Rajesh Kumar: Integration dashboard snapshot looks flaky in CI (panel ordering). Can you add a deterministic sort in the snapshot serializer?
Maya Patel: Fixed serializer ordering in tests and retriggered CI.
Sofia Martinez: Approved - tests green and docs look good.
release_notes: Adds token-level KV cache metrics, new Grafana dashboard (Token KV Cost & Latency Overview), route-level adaptive token-latency alerts with refractory windows, improved tracing spans to surface cache hits/misses, and runbook updates. Metrics are behind feature flag observability.kv_token_metrics; rollout instructions included in the runbook.
